Duties include general upkeep such as pressure washing, window cleaning, trash removal, and routine cleaning tasks. Porter also support event setup and cleanup when necessary and respond to cleanliness concerns as they arise. The position requires reliability, attention to detail, and the ability to work professionally and courteously with property staff, tenants, and visitors. Key Responsibilities Ensures all common areas, including sidewalks, lobbies, restrooms, and public spaces are kept clean and presentable. Completes daily cleaning and janitorial tasks as assigned by the Senior Operations Manager, Janitorial. Pressure washes areas as assigned by management. Reports to assigned location in the approved ParkX Porter uniform. Reports to assigned location before the start of the work shift. Ensures compliance with all safety regulations and cleaning standards. Exhibits a professional and courteous demeanor with all site visitors. Acknowledges, greets, and interacts professionally with property staff and guests, using appropriate protocols. Assists management teams with special cleaning or maintenance requests as needed. Always maintains a neat and orderly janitorial closet and storage areas, free of debris and hazards. Completes any required end-of-shift documentation and ensures proper transfer of responsibilities to the next shift. Helps with setup and breakdown

jobs.title: Full-Time Supervisor de Limpieza (Jueves a Lunes, 11PM-6AM)
jobs.description_text: Descripción General del Puesto: El Supervisor de Limpieza de ParkX es responsable de mantener la limpieza en las áreas comunes de los sitios asignados. Sus funciones incluyen el mantenimiento general, como lavado a presión, limpieza de ventanas, recolección de basura y tareas de limpieza rutinarias. El portero también apoya en la preparación y limpieza de eventos cuando sea necesario y responde a las inquietudes de limpieza conforme surgen. El puesto requiere responsabilidad, atención al detalle y la capacidad de trabajar de manera profesional y cortés con el personal de la propiedad, los residentes y los visitantes. #WeShowUp Responsabilidades: Garantiza que todas las áreas comunes, incluidos aceras, vestíbulos, baños y espacios públicos, se mantengan limpias y presentables. Completa las tareas diarias de limpieza y mantenimiento según lo asignado por el Gerente Senior de Operaciones, Limpieza. Realiza lavado a presión en las áreas asignadas por la gerencia. Se presenta en la ubicación asignada usando el uniforme aprobado de ParkX Porter. Llega a la ubicación asignada antes del inicio del turno de trabajo. Garantiza el cumplimiento de todas las normas de seguridad y estándares de limpieza. Mantiene una actitud profesional y cortés con todos los visitantes del sitio. Reconoce, saluda e interactúa de manera profesional con el personal de la propiedad y los invitados, siguiendo los protocolos correspondientes. Apoya a los equipos de gestión con solicitudes especiales de limpiez

jobs.title: Data Center Power Generation and Microgrids Engineer
jobs.description_text: About the role Training and serving frontier AI models requires compute infrastructure at a scale and density that pushes past what conventional data center designs were built to handle. The loads involved are large enough — and arrive fast enough — that utility supply alone often can't meet the need on the timeline required, and the step-load behavior of large accelerator clusters creates power-quality and ride-through demands that conventional backup-generation designs weren't built for. Anthropic's Data Center Infrastructure team is responsible for solving that problem: delivering facilities that can be energized early, ride through grid disturbances, and present a well-behaved load at the point of interconnection (POI). As a Data Center Power Generation & Microgrids Engineer, you'll own the behind-the-meter generation and storage architecture for Anthropic's data center portfolio. That means the on-site generation fleet — reciprocating engine gensets, gas turbines, fuel cells — and the battery energy storage systems that buffer load steps and provide ride-through. It means the microgrid layer that ties them together: islanding and resynchronization, black-start, load-shedding, and generation dispatch. And it means the grid side: interconnection studies and agreements, IEEE 1547/2800 compliance, and power quality at the point of interconnection. jobs.description_text: About the role As an Integrity and Authenticity Policy Manager, you will be responsible for developing, refining, and maintaining policies that prevent the misuse of AI systems for deception, manipulation, and unauthorized monitoring at scale. You will serve as the policy owner for risks related to inauthentic behavior, influence activity, surveillance, and the profiling of individuals and groups, and you will help shape policy frameworks across several areas, including authenticity, information integrity, and privacy and surveillance. Your initial focus will be on translating the Integrity and Authenticity risk framework into clear, enforceable policies, ensuring policy language addresses emerging threats identified by partner teams, and establishing guidelines that enable consistent enforcement decisions. Many of the most serious harms in this space begin with upstream steps that look routine on their own, such as compiling records about a person, automating account creation, or sorting users by inferred identity. Part of your work will be defining where those steps become prohibited. The role will expand as AI capabilities advance. Safety is core to our mission. You will help ensure our products cannot be used to deceive people at scale, monitor and profile people without their knowledge or consent, or sort and target populations based on sensitive characteristics. jobs.description_text: About the role Reinforcement learning is how Claude learns to reason, write code, and act autonomously over long horizons. At frontier scale, an RL run is an unusually demanding distributed system. Training, sampling, and environment execution run concurrently across a large fleet of accelerators and hosts, exchange data continuously, and have to keep making progress while hardware fails, load shifts, and the research changes underneath them. How well that system holds together determines how much of our compute turns into learning, and how quickly the team can try the next idea. As a Research Engineer on the Distributed Systems team within RL Engineering, you'll work on whatever part of that system is the current limit. That might be scheduling and placement, data movement between components, running large numbers of sandboxed environments, storage and checkpointing, networking, fault tolerance, autoscaling, or the observability that tells us what a run is actually doing. We're looking for generalists: engineers who can move between these layers, reason from first principles about a system they haven't seen before, and pick the problem that matters most rather than the one closest to their prior experience. Our system changes as fast as the research does, correctness under failure matters as much as throughput, and the best solutions often come from understanding the ML workload well enough to know which guarantees it actually needs. jobs.location_raw: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA
jobs.description_text: About the role Reinforcement learning is how Claude learns to reason, write code, and act autonomously over long horizons. The RL Scaling team works on how RL scales: what happens to throughput, stability, and learning efficiency as models get larger, episodes get longer, and compute grows by orders of magnitude, and what has to change in our algorithms and systems to keep getting returns from that scale. This role sits squarely across research and engineering. You'll develop next-generation architectures and RL algorithms, take them from a small-scale result to a frontier-scale run, and understand every place they behave differently along the way. jobs.title: Staff / Senior Physical Security Systems Engineer
jobs.description_text: About the role Data Center Security Engineering (DCSE) secures Anthropic's data center footprint; this role covers how the sites are designed and built to be secure. Much of that footprint is designed and built with partners, so a site's security is decided early: in what Anthropic hands the people who build it, and in how rigorously the delivered systems are tested against it. You'll design and specify the physical security systems for a site: perimeter and vehicle barriers, intrusion detection, video, security lighting, and the site penetrations and utility entry points that bypass them. Design firms and integrators produce the site drawings and install; you specify, review, and verify. You'll write the performance requirement and verification method behind each control, review every site design against them at each stage with redlines a design team can act on, test in the field that what was built performs as specified, and re-verify post-acceptance changes. This is a foundational role. You'll own Anthropic's physical security reference design package (typical details, reference drawings, schedules, and test procedures) in the form partners build from, and keep it current against each site's threat basis and the sites actually being built. You'll set the technical position for a site and decide what applies where; where a requirement can't be met as written, you'll engineer the compensating control and document the deviation. jobs.description_text: About the role Frontier AI is on track to be among the most consequential and most adversarially-targeted technology in the world. The capability curve is steep, the adversaries who want these systems are extremely well-resourced, and the security bar this will eventually require is well beyond where the industry operates today. Incremental hardening alone is not going to close that gap, so we need breakthroughs and a group of people to go find them. Security Labs is that team. We run a portfolio of high-risk, high-expected-value security projects: the work that seems impractical until someone optimistic and stubborn enough actually tries it. Projects run on the order of weeks rather than quarters, and each one is either handed off to the Anthropic team that will own it in production or wound down with a writeup of what we learned. We expect a meaningful fraction of our bets not to land. This team is intentionally scrappy and ambitious. We're intentionally iterating fast on high-risk research bets and we expect a meaningful fraction not to land. If a 30% project success rate sounds uncomfortable, or uncharted and chaotic territory isn’t both frightening and exciting, this probably isn't the right fit. There are other places in Anthropic Security doing important work with more structure, less risk, and more certain paths to positive outcomes. You will review statements of work and support the scoping and planning of large projects with Sales, build that skill across the team of technical program managers, find efficiencies in how we deliver, and grow program managers at every level as demand grows. You'll be accountable for delivering a large portfolio of enterprise projects, and for the team that makes sure customers have a great experience with our products. jobs.title: Electrical Component Engineer I (Onsite)
jobs.description_text: Your Impact This role sits at the intersection of engineering and supply chain, owning component strategy from design through full product lifecycle. You will directly influence product cost, supply resilience, and scalability by driving component selection, supplier strategy, and lifecycle risk management across Axon’s product portfolio. What You’ll Do Location: Scottsdale, Arizona (HQ) Reports to: D irector of Category Management Direct Reports: none Partner with design engineering teams early in the NPI development process to influence component selection by leveraging your industry experience. Establish strong relationships with manufacturers and their associated representatives in the electronics industry to understand product roadmaps and availability to support current and future product development. Work with the sourcing team to develop and ramp component sources for new products and support the NPI team’s efforts to ensure components are purchased in a timely manner for engineering development builds. Leverage your technical expertise and industry knowledge to select key strategic components to support product scalability for 5+ year lifecycles. Assist the respective Category Managers and cross-functional category teams in developing and executing multidimensional commodity strategies that support the NPI work stream with an emphasis on cost optimization, time to market, technology, quality, supply continuity, supply chain consolidation, service and risk mitigation.

By leveraging your technical acumen and problem-solving skills, you will be instrumental in identifying and overcoming RF challenges, ensuring robust designs that operate seamlessly in diverse and demanding environments. You will collaborate with cross-functional teams and global partners to verify and refine wireless designs, using state-of-the-art tools and methodologies. Your work will directly contribute to the development of reliable, high-performance solutions that serve Law Enforcement, Public Safety, and the communities they protect. Through your efforts, you will help deliver transformative technologies that empower public safety professionals and redefine industry standards. What You’ll Do Design and implement test plans to evaluate the performance of wirelessly connected devices, ensuring they meet stringent product and regulatory requirements.
